citation: Kuhn et al. (2025). AMR-Wind: A performance-portable, high-fidelity flow solver for wind farm simulations. Wind Energy. https://doi.org/10.1002/we.70010
description: Kynema-SGF is a structured-grid fluid solver maintained by Lawrence Berkeley, Sandia and the National Laboratory of the Rockies for wind-energy research. It contains an incompressible flow model on adaptive AMReX meshes, including atmospheric boundary-layer simulations and actuator representations of turbines. Inputs describe the computational domain, forcing and turbine configuration; outputs describe evolving flow fields and wakes. Spatial and temporal resolution follow the chosen mesh and simulation steps. Free BSD-3-Clause source is available in C++17 with documented builds for CPU and GPU systems. A limitation is the need to match mesh resolution, turbulence assumptions and computing resources to the wind-farm problem. The code was previously named AMR-Wind. It supports energy-infrastructure design and flow simulations, and can couple with the distinct near-body solver Kynema-UGF (model-kynema-ugf). The maintainers cite separate AMR-Wind and ExaWind method papers. No software was built or executed.
